name: imagodei
description: Identity and presence — humans, attestations, agency, relationships. Grounds the protocol in demonstrated capability and community trust.

human.description: A person in the network. The foundational identity entity — every other identity concept (role, contributor, attestation) attaches to a human. Agent-scoped: each agent has exactly one human record.

role.description: A functional role a human can hold — steward, elder, reviewer, facilitator. Roles are derived via link from identity to capability. They gate what actions are available and what governance weight a human carries.

contributor.description: A contributor presence in the content graph. When a human creates, curates, or reviews content, they establish presence as a contributor. Presence is the bridge between identity (imagodei) and stewardship standing (shefa). Notarized: contributor records are DHT-gossipped.

IDENTIFIES.description: A human identity identifies a contributor presence. The link between who you are and what you've done in the content graph.

IDENTIFIED_BY.description: Reverse of IDENTIFIES — a contributor presence is identified by a human.

ASSIGNED_TO.description: A role is assigned to a human. Grants capabilities within a scope.

GRANTS.description: A role grants capability to a contributor. The mechanism by which roles expand what a contributor can do.

SCOPED_TO.description: A role is scoped to a collective. Roles don't float — they exist within a governance context.

STEWARDS.description: A contributor stewards content. The curation relationship that builds affinity over time.

ATTESTS.description: A contributor attests to the capability or identity of another. The trust primitive — community-verified claims replace institutional credentials.

PARTICIPATES_IN.description: A human participates in a collective. Membership in a governance community.

identity-created.description: Emitted when a new human identity is established in the network. The foundational event that makes all other protocol interactions possible.

presence-established.description: Emitted when a human establishes contributor presence by creating or claiming authorship. The bridge from identity to stewardship.

attestation-granted.description: Emitted when a contributor attests to another's capability or identity. The trust primitive — community verification replacing institutional credentials.

attestation-revoked.description: Emitted when a previously granted attestation is revoked. Negative signal — reduces trust standing. Required for the system to self-correct.

agency-progressed.description: Emitted when a human advances in agency stage (visitor -> observer -> participant -> steward -> elder). Agency progression gates capability expansion.

relationship-formed.description: Emitted when a trust relationship is formed between humans or contributors. Relationships are the graph edges that carry attestations and governance weight.

identity-retention.description: Human identity remains active — person continues to participate, contribute, or engage with the network over time

attestation-accuracy.description: Attested claims hold up over time — humans attested as capable demonstrate that capability in downstream work

identity-abandonment.description: Identity created but never meaningfully used — person registered but did not participate, contribute, or form relationships

attestation-inaccuracy.description: Attested claims do not hold up — humans attested as capable fail in downstream work they were attested for. The negative feedback that keeps attestation gates honest.
